title: Playability report
description: Whether a built game can be played and read by a first-time player, measured from outside: a bot drives the production build with real pointer and key input on desktop and mobile viewports, reads its play probe (shared/play-probe.schema.json) before and after each input, and inspects rendered frames. Every check names what was measured and the bar from the design's experience contract (core/reference/experience-rules.yaml) or core/reference/visual-quality.yaml. This is automation evidence: it proves the game is playable and visible, and it never stands in for what first-time players understand (a kill criterion measured from people).

commit.description: The commit that was built and played.

measurement_class.description: Who played: a bot through the play probe. Never a first-time player.

projects.description: The viewports it was played on.

id.description: e.g. probe.present, start.objective, idle.grace, act.acknowledged, win.reachable, lose.reachable, restart.works, entities.visible, frames.luminance.

summary.description: What was measured, and against which bar.

frames.description: Captured frames, kept beside the run as evidence.

lit_share.description: Share of the frame's pixels lit (core/reference/visual-quality.yaml frames.lit_luminance).
